title: Abdul El-Sayed Talks to Zeteo About His Historic Victory
author: Mehdi Hasan
content:
Despite the record outside spending, the Islamophobia, and the Haley Stevens
betrayal, progressive candidate **Abdul El-Sayed** won his Michigan Senate
race by seven points on Tuesday, and in doing so, became the first Muslim
elected to the Senate in U.S. history.

Now, in a special '**Mehdi Unfiltered** ' interview, El-Sayed joined **Mehdi**
on set in DC today to reflect on his historic victory, explain how he plans to
hold the Trump administration accountable for its corruption, and reveal
whether there are conversations to replace Chuck Schumer as Senate Majority
Leader.

"**I 'm looking for a leadership that is ready for action on day one**," El-
Sayed tells Mehdi. "**I 'm hoping that somebody is going to come out there and
help to build that kind of movement to try and get us to that point where we
lead differently**."

During the interview, the two also discuss "**habibi** " J.D. Vance, who will
now have to swear in El-Sayed to the Senate in January, and react to the vice
president's own provocative analysis of why Republicans were **" smoked**" in
the midterms.

"**This is what happens when you rubber stamp the dumbest possible president
in American history, and then this man ruins your political future, and then
now, all of a sudden, you 're trying to pretend like you had nothing to do
with it,**" El-Sayed says.

The new senator-elect from Michigan tells Mehdi about his plan to persuade
Donald Trump to sign off on a Medicare-for-All bill and whether or not he
received a concession call from vanquished Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

But is El-Sayed gearing up to run against Vance in 2028? Is it too soon to
even ask? You can guess that Mehdi couldn't resist!

**Paid subscribers** can watch the full almost half-hour interview above to
hear El-Sayed's answer, as well as his response to all the racist media
coverage of his use of the words "**Inshallah** " and "**Alhamdulillah** " in
his victory speech.
